verdict_reason: Part 5 does change budgets at TP3, but the replay predicts no gain anywhere. It trims draft rows that candidate-50's tp3-switched grid prices below the tokens they carry. Every step-time model built on that grid predicts lower throughput at c1, c4 and c8, and at c1 and c8 the loss is beyond the 0.35-0.4% A/A floor. The scale drives c4 and c8: at c8, -1.2% to -1.3% on the grid step alone and -3.1% to -3.3% on the served step. The dead-row floor drives c1: -0.9% to -1.0% on the grid step and -1.0% to -1.2% on the served step. #986's blend calibrated on the 2026-10-18 row-cost A/B also predicts a loss: -0.3% to -1.2% at c1 and -0.2% to -1.3% at c8. Only #986's tp4-ring serving regression taken alone (model B) predicts a c1 gain (+1.0% to +1.1%). It prices a wasted row at 1.98 ms, against the TP3 grid's 0.17 ms a row, and the A/B-calibrated blend gives it at most 43% weight at c1. Recommendation (the coordinator decides): leave 957-p5 out of candidate-57. If it is carried, the no957p5 overlay supports an attribution control on the same image.

conflict.0789_971_r1: _step_cost prices rows past HIGH_ROW_COST_KNEE (16) with single_req_tile_spill_scale = SINGLE_REQ_TILE_SPILL_SCALE (2.0) when num_sampling_requests <= 1, else high_row_cost_scale (HIGH_ROW_COST_SCALE 0.55); get_num_tokens passes num_sampling_requests
conflict.part_5: picks HIGH_ROW_COST_SCALE_TP3 (0.85) for self.high_row_cost_scale in __init__ when tp_size == 3 (written on 1107, where that scale priced every step) and floors the calibrated dead-row threshold at MIN_CALIBRATED_DEAD_ROWS_TAU_TP3 (0.12)

composition.decision: HIGH_ROW_COST_SCALE_TP3 replaces only the multi-request scale (self.high_row_cost_scale, num_sampling_requests > 1). A single sampling request keeps #971 round 1's SINGLE_REQ_TILE_SPILL_SCALE = 2.0 on every TP size. At c1 the effective scale is therefore max(2.0, 0.85) = 2.0. No TP3-specific single-request scale is added.
why: The two scales model different things. 0.55 and 0.85 are the shared-weight-tile discount for rows past the 16-row MMA tile when several requests coalesce. 2.0 is the single-request penalty for spilling the 17th row into a second MMA wave and the 24-row graph. #971 round 1 measured that step at TP3 (initial c1 copy step, 24-row graph to 16-row graph, -5.52%, Welch95 [-9.0, -7.6] ms) with the 2.0 scale.

Part 5 was written on 1107, where one scale priced every step, so on its own base it replaced the c1 price too. Carried that way onto candidate-54, it would undo #971 round 1 at TP3. The fixed cell c1_copy_0.95x16 gives 15 drafts and 16 rows with this patch at TP3, and 16 drafts and 17 rows if 0.85 also priced single requests (raw/out/replay-*.json, deterministic).
There is no TP3 evidence for a different single-request scale. A multiplied scale (2.0 x 0.85 / 0.55) would be a new, unmeasured constant.
A c1 step with a prefill in the batch has two sampling requests, so it uses the multi-request branch, TP3's 0.85 included. That is #971 round 1's own definition, unchanged.

dead_row_floor.why: The recipe sets SPARK_DS41F_DSPARK_DEAD_ROWS_TAU=0.2 and adaptive_verification_row_cost 0.035, and the model runner passes calibrated_confidence = (estimator _refits > 0 and the confidence head is used). Once the estimator has refit, candidate-54's effective_dead_rows_tau is min(0.2, 2*0.035/(1+3*0.035)) = 0.0633. With part 5 at TP3 it is min(0.2, max(0.12, 0.0633)) = 0.12 (the replay's managers report 0.0633 and 0.1200). Before the first refit both return 0.2. So the floor is not inert; it raises the host admission cut and the device dead-row cut at TP3.
dead_row_floor.kept: yes. The deployment-only rule leaves out only what does nothing here, and the floor acts. It is also the whole of part 5's effect at c1, where the replay predicts a loss.
dead_row_floor.where_it_binds: c1 only, in effect: 22-29% of c1 steps change budget, 1.3-1.9% of c4 steps, about 0.01% of c8 steps. At c4 and c8 the budget's own cut is already above 0.12.

replay.what: a policy replay of the real AdaptiveVerificationManager. Candidate-54's adaptive_verification.py and the rebased part 5's were loaded by path in spark-ds41f:candidate-50 with candidate-54's 36 changed files mounted, so every vllm import is candidate-54's. Each manager was built through its own __init__ (small CUDA buffers) with get_tp_group patched to world size 3 or 4. get_num_tokens drove each step; one manager per arm persisted across the steps, so its idle-explore counter carries as in serving.
replay.recipe_inputs: 5 drafts, 16 verification steps (copy drafter on), row cost 0.035, SPARK_DS41F_DSPARK_DEAD_ROWS_TAU=0.2 (env), calibrated confidence (lambda: True), max_total_logits = get_max_chunk_logits(129280) (never binds)
replay.acceptance_profile: #986 round 1's served profile (candidate-47/receipts/rework/pr-986-r1): its fitted two-component logit-normal confidence model per concurrency (theta from replay-seed0.json and replay-seed1.json), its step sampler (served requests a step plus one 21-token prefill at the served prompt rate), and calibrated acceptance (expected tokens = admitted survival). c4 has no served record: it uses c8's theta at half c8's requests and prompt rate, and c1's theta as a sensitivity (c4-theta-c1).

step_time.grid: candidate-50's tp3-switched screen grid, two boots (receipts/references/candidate-50-no1009-tp3-switched-screen{,-again}/grid.json), fitted at 4K: t = a + b n + c1 min(R,16) + c2 max(R-16,0); rows padded to the TP3 capture ladder [1,2,3,4,6,8,12,16,20,24,28,32,40,48] (eager above 48)

step_time.model_A: grid + constant served overhead, anchored so candidate-54's replayed mean equals candidate-50's tp3-switched served step: c1 1000/26.293 = 38.03 ms (single-stream), c8 1000/8.650 = 115.61 ms (screen c8, two boots); c4 overhead interpolated in requests (49.5 ms)
step_time.model_B: #986's tp4-ring per-batch serving regression (intercept + ms/token + ms/wasted row). A sensitivity only: it is TP4's and prices a wasted row at 1.98 ms at c1 and 0.46 ms at c8.
step_time.model_M: #986's blend w A + (1 - w) B, with its weights calibrated on the 2026-10-18 row-cost A/B (c1 w 0.57/0.86/1.0, c8 w 0.0/0.01/0.30). The weights were fitted with TP4's model A, so applying them at TP3 is an approximation.

why_no_gain: The grid prices rows far below the budget's own price. At TP3 a row costs 0.170 ms up to 16 rows and 0.220 ms past 16, on an 18.6 ms fixed step: 0.9% and 1.2% of the step. The recipe's row cost is 3.5% of the step. At c8 (about 26 rows) candidate-54 already charges a row past 16 about 1.1% of its modelled step, against the grid's 0.9% of the GPU step and 0.19% of the served step. Part 5's 0.85 raises that to about 1.6%, so it trims rows whose survival (about 0.2-0.3) is worth more tokens than the 0.22 ms they cost.

At c1 the floor rejects slots with survival between 0.063 and 0.12. On the grid, such a slot pays for itself above roughly 0.02 survival (tokens 2.3 x 0.17 ms / 19.3 ms GPU step), or 0.01 on the served step.

The PR's premise, that TP3 rows past the knee cost more than TP4's, does not show in the grids. TP3-switched rows cost 0.170 and 0.220 ms; TP4-switched rows cost 0.255 and 0.272 ms (0.9% against 1.7% of the step). Neither grid shows the knee discount: the slope ratio past 16 is 1.29 at TP3 and 1.06 at TP4.
At TP3 a c8 step of 40 rows runs the 40-row graph. The ladder holds 40, so the PR's '40 rows -> padded to 48' does not apply here.
